## Background and Recording: "Bad Habit" (Steve Lacy)

**Creation and early version**
- Lacy first recorded the song in June 2021, using a beat he made with drums he had used before. He later called writing it a turning point, saying it was "the start of this renaissance of the separation between [past] Steve and [present] Steve." (Source: Jeremy Gordon, "Steve Lacy Is a New Kind of Guitar Hero," *GQ*, June 23, 2022, https://www.gq.com/story/gq-hype-steve-lacy)
- The article does not give a citation for the drum-reuse detail.

**Fousheé freestyle**
- Lacy played the instrumental for singer Fousheé, who later worked with him on several songs for *Gemini Rights*. The two spent about 20 minutes freestyling over the beat, which led to verses and a chorus melody. (Source: Shaad D'Souza, "'My mom thinks I'm doing drugs but I'm at home baking cookies': Steve Lacy on his breakout year," *The Guardian*, December 22, 2022, https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year)

**Revisions over the following year**
- Lacy changed other elements over the next year, including the ending breakdown, the drums, and the chorus. (Same *Guardian* source.)
- Songwriter Diana Gordon wrote part of the ending. (Same *Guardian* source.)
- John Carroll Kirby and Matthew Castellanos are also credited as co-writers. (Source: Rania Aniftos, "Here Are the Lyrics to Steve Lacy's 'Bad Habit'," *Billboard*, July 26, 2022, https://www.billboard.com/music/lyrics/steve-lacy-bad-habit-lyrics-1235118457/)
- Kirby's role is listed as "songwriting, additional synths" in the album booklet. (Source: *Gemini Rights* album booklet, RCA Records/Sony Music.)
- Lacy said the song was finished a week before he submitted *Gemini Rights* to RCA Records. (Same *Guardian* source.)
- The *Billboard* chartbreaker interview (Cydney Lee, August 3, 2022) also covers the song's development: https://www.billboard.com/music/features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-billboard-august-2022-chartbreaker-interview-1235121728/

**Production and mixing**
- Lacy produced the song. Neal Pogue mixed it at his Hot Purple Petting Zoo studio in Los Angeles, and Mike Bozzi of Bernie Grundman Mastering mastered it. Pogue's mix made the guitar riff the song's main focus. (Sources: *Billboard*, October 3, 2022, https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/steve-lacy-bad-habit-hot-100-sam-smith-kim-petras-glorilla-cardi-b-1235149114/; Paul Tingen, "Inside Track: Steve Lacy 'Bad Habit'," *Sound on Sound*, December 2022, https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/inside-track-steve-lacy-bad-habit)

**Versions**
- Album version: 3:52. Radio version: 2:45.
- Fan-made sped-up versions became popular on TikTok. One was used in over 430,000 videos, which led RCA to release an official sped-up version. Lacy first called the idea "gross" but agreed, hoping it would help the song reach No. 1. (Guardian source above; Conor Murray, *Forbes*, January 18, 2023, https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2023/01/18/why-sped-up-music-from-sza-steve-lacy-and-many-more-took-over-tiktok-and-became-a-key-marketing-strategy/)

**Release**
- Released June 29, 2022, through RCA Records, as the second single from *Gemini Rights*. The album came out July 15, 2022. (Source: Cydney Lee, *Billboard*, August 3, 2022, linked above.)

**Chart performance**
- The song entered the *Billboard* Hot 100 at No. 100 in July 2022, when it first went viral on TikTok. It was Lacy's first chart entry.
- It reached No. 1 on the Hot 100 on the chart dated October 3, 2022, replacing Harry Styles's "As It Was," which had held the top spot for 15 weeks. This was Lacy's first No. 1. (Sources: Gary Trust, *Billboard*, October 3, 2022, linked above; Ben Sisario, *The New York Times*, October 3, 2022, https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/03/arts/music/steve-lacy-bad-habit-billboard-chart.html)
- On the chart issued September 10, 2022, it became the first song to top both the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and Hot Rock & Alternative Songs charts. (Kevin Rutherford, *Billboard*, September 6, 2022, https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/steve-lacy-bad-habit-tops-rb-hip-hop-songs-alternative-1235135263/)

**Note:** The article's Background section is a secondary summary, and several details above rely on interviews it cites. Check the original sources before relying on exact wording or dates.

**Source:** Paul Tingen, "Inside Track: Steve Lacy 'Bad Habit'," *Sound On Sound*, December 2022. The article is part of the "Secrets Of The Mix Engineers" series.

**Speaker:** Only mix engineer Neal Pogue is quoted. Steve Lacy is not directly quoted, so his wishes are reported through Pogue.

**Lacy's direction and the mix**
- Lacy wanted the vocals placed in a certain space, not too loud, and blended with the music. Pogue says this matched his own preference: "Steve wants his vocals in a certain space, not too loud."
- Pogue describes the guitar as the focus of "Bad Habit," with bass, vocals, drums and synths supporting it.
- Lacy's notes after the first mix pass were minimal. Pogue recalls requests to raise the guitar slightly and lower the vocal, which surprised him. The article quotes the request as "Turn up the guitar a little bit more."

**Mix process**
- Pogue starts with the drums and bass, then the guitars, then keys, then vocals and harmonies.
- He builds sessions with colour-coded tracks and says he creates each mix from scratch, without templates.
- He treats Gemini Rights as an album-level project but approaches each song individually.

**Processing on "Bad Habit"** (as described by Pogue)
- Kick: Waves SSL EQ.
- Bass: UAD Fairchild compressor, then Waves SSL EQ, then Waves SSL EV2 and McDSP CB101.
- Main guitar: Waves Infected Mushroom plug-in, Waves Scheps 73 EQ, Kilohearts Chorus, and an API 550A EQ and Soundtoys Decapitator on a guitar aux track.
- Synths: Infected Mushroom and API on each of the three or four synth parts, and an Infected Mushroom Wider on a Moog track.
- Lead vocal: UAD Fairchild 670, Waves API 550A, Waves SSL Channel and Soundtoys MicroShift. Background vocals received little processing.
- Master bus: Waves L2 and iZotope Ozone (9, then 10). Mastering for Gemini Rights was by Mike Bozzi at Bernie Grundman Mastering.

**Studio and monitoring**
- Pogue's studio is HotPurplePettingZoo in Los Angeles. He works mainly in the box on Pro Tools with an Avid HD I/O, and has a Universal Audio LA-610 for vocals.
- He monitors on JBL 708P and Reftone speakers.

- It does not discuss other tracks on Gemini Rights.

  - 2021년 6월 처음 녹음했다.
  - Fousheé와 약 20분간 프리스타일하며 벌스와 후렴 멜로디가 나왔다.
  - 이후 1년 동안 드럼, 후렴, 엔딩을 고쳤다.
  - 엔딩 일부는 Diana Gordon이 썼다.
  - 앨범을 RCA에 제출하기 1주 전에 완성했다.
- 이 곡을 "renaissance of the separation between [past] Steve and [present] Steve"의 시작이라고 한 발언도 GQ를 거친 재인용이다.

**C6. 작사 방식** [직접 발언·원문 확인]
- "blurt words out … edit, edit, edit" [S2]
- 기자는 이를 래퍼 같은 프리스타일 방식이라고 서술했다.

**C7. Bad Habit 믹스** [직접 발언(믹싱 엔지니어)·원문 확인]
- 믹싱 엔지니어 Neal Pogue의 설명 [S6]:
  - 이 곡의 중심은 기타다.
  - Lacy는 보컬이 "not too loud"하게 들어가길 원했다.
  - 첫 믹스 뒤 Lacy가 기타를 키우고 보컬을 줄여 달라고 요청했다.
- **한계**: Bad Habit에 한정된 설명이다. Lacy 본인의 말은 인용되지 않았다.

**C8. 영향원 목록** [공식 문서(레이블 홍보문)·원문 확인]
- 보도자료는 Caetano Veloso, André 3000의 *The Love Below*, 비틀스, Sly Stone을 영향원으로 든다 [S9].
- Lacy가 직접 밝힌 영향인지는 확인하지 못했다. 홍보문을 옮긴 여러 페이지는 독립된 근거로 세지 않았다.

**샘플**: 위키백과에는 샘플 표기가 없다 [S3]. 이 조사에서 확인한 샘플·인용 관계는 없다. 그렇다고 샘플이 없다는 뜻은 아니다(④ 참조).
